reason: The load tray looks like the foundation for testing and balancing a load on the tethered tile.
expectation: The tray will attach to the lift test so it can carry a load.

effect: The tray is attached, so the lift test is ready for a load.
reaction: The straightforward fitting makes the next test clearer.
reason: The off-centre block should reveal whether the loaded tray tips before I try to balance it.
expectation: The block will load the tray unevenly and show how the tile behaves.

effect: The uneven load makes the tray tilt, so it needs balancing.
reaction: The test clearly shows why lift alone is not enough.
reason: The sliding counterweight should balance the off-centre load.
expectation: Adjusting the counterweight will bring the tray closer to level.

effect: The counterweight levels the tray, but the added load requires more lift.
reaction: Seeing the trade-off between balance and total load is useful.
reason: The current controller should let me adjust the lift for the heavier tray.
expectation: The controller will allow enough lift for the balanced load.

effect: The balanced tray now has an adjustable lift controller.
reason: The goal calls for a reliable stop, so the power-cut switch is the next clear addition.
expectation: The switch will provide a way to cut power and stop the lift.

effect: The power-cut switch overrides the controller, and the module is disconnected and reset for moving.
reaction: The override makes the stop's purpose clear.
reason: The lifting sling looks like the next piece needed to move the module safely with the crane.
expectation: The sling will attach to the module so the crane can lift it.

effect: The sling attaches to the crane rather than directly to the module; the crane is now ready to lift it.
reaction: I expected the other attachment order, but the compatibility feedback made it clear.
reason: The prepared crane and stopped module are the remaining pieces for moving the lift module.
expectation: The crane will use the sling to lift and move the stopped module.

effect: The crane removed the complete balanced module from the stand, with the test weights left behind and the counterweight centred for the empty tray.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the tested parts become one movable module.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the off-centre load and correcting it with the sliding counterweight made the balance problem and the cost of added weight clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the tray was straightforward but less informative than the later tests.

surprise.text: The counterweight levelled the tray but also increased the total load, requiring more lift.

arbitrary.text: The sling attachment order was not obvious to me: I tried the module first, but it needed to go on the crane.

continue.text: I would continue: the balance test and power-cut override made the invented lift tile part of a practical construction problem, and I would be curious to see how the module supports the fair.
